correct_completion: the children ran out to play.
full_sentence: The rain having stopped, the children ran out to play.
acceptable_variants: the children went outside to play.
the kids rushed out into the garden.

options.text: so the children ran out to play.
options.why_wrong: 'So' introduces a result clause. Placed after an absolute clause it creates a clash, because the absolute clause needs a main clause directly after it.

options.text: the children ran out to play.
although the children ran out to play.
options.why_wrong: 'Although' introduces a concessive subordinate clause, so the sentence would have no main clause and the contrast does not fit the meaning.

options.text: the children running out to play.
options.why_wrong: This is a participle phrase with no finite verb, so the sentence remains incomplete.

grammar_focus: Absolute clauses with a having-participle subject
explanation: An absolute clause has its own subject, here 'the rain', and a non-finite verb. It is followed directly by the main clause, with no conjunction between them. Options that add a conjunction or leave the main clause out do not complete the structure correctly.
translation: Gdy deszcz przestał padać, dzieci wybiegły bawić się na dwór.
